text:
leo: trying the Python quickstart sample. curl to /v1/generate works, but python sdk raises 402 PaymentRequired: 'workspace_not_linked'. Really confusing because console shows billing set up.

onboarding-bot: Hello! Workspace 'team-rocket' created. Reminder: attach a billing method to the workspace to call paid endpoints.

claudia: Can you paste the snippet? Also which key is in your .env vs your shell?

leo: snippet: `from redwood import Client\nclient = Client()\nclient.generate(\"hey\")` I used docker-compose to run sample, and the container log shows `REDWOOD_KEY` present but SDK logs 402.

jun: SDK looks for REDWOOD_API_KEY or REDWOOD_KEY? We standardized on REDWOOD_API_KEY but left backward compat checks in Node only. Python might only read REDWOOD_API_KEY.

leo: Inside container `env` shows REDWOOD_KEY=sk_live_xxx but no REDWOOD_API_KEY. If I run `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$REDWOOD_KEY` locally and re-run python it works.

claudia: Ah, docker-compose env_file v2 behavior on mac strips env if you use `env_file:` and an entrypoint script that runs `env -i`. Sample entrypoint was sanitizing env for safety.

infra: We should avoid breaking env propagation in samples. Also SDK should attempt common legacy var names before failing with a 402 that blames billing.

devex: Action items: (1) change python SDK to accept REDWOOD_KEY fallback, (2) make 402 error message include "env var not found / using workspace key" when applicable, (3) update sample docker-compose to not drop env or document the entrypoint behavior, (4) add quick troubleshooting FAQ about env vs workspace keys.

leo: Filed a tiny PR to the sample repo to stop clearing env and added a note in README about env var names. PR link: https://github.com/redwood/sample-app/pull/123

claudia: Also adding a small startup log: `Using API key from REDWOOD_API_KEY` so users see which var was used.

leo: First successful call after the fix. Leaving this here in case others hit the same docker+env var trap. :rocket:
